dedupe_keys.name: geomagnetic magnetotelluric and power network data for the april 2023 storm in alberta

description: This data set holds everything needed to reproduce models of geomagnetically induced currents in the Alberta power network during the geomagnetic storm of 23-24 April 2023. It was published on Zenodo in January 2024 by Darcy Cordell, Martyn Unsworth and Ian Mann, with raw data from the University of Alberta CARISMA magnetometer network, Natural Resources Canada and the US Geological Survey geomagnetism programmes, and supports their Space Weather paper that compares modelled currents with Hall probe measurements. It contains magnetometer records for the storm from western Canada and the north-western United States; magnetotelluric data from 526 sites collected by the University of Alberta over about 20 years plus older LITHOPROBE sites, with a 3-D conductivity model and forward-modelled responses; and power network data with substation locations, earthing resistances and transmission line routing. Coverage is Alberta, Canada. Files are zipped data archives and an Excel workbook, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: it covers one storm, and the network data describe the grid as modelled for the study. Simulation uses are validating geomagnetically induced current models, geoelectric field estimation and space weather risk assessment of transmission grids. Related records: data-great-britain-grid-gic-open-data is a comparable British data set, and model-powermodelsgmd-jl can compute such currents.
